description: One of the two great empires flanking Marrenhold, and the Vharr Empire's opposite in almost every way. The Niven, the pale folk of the dead north, hold the northern expanses -- reaches so harsh that no other creatures can thrive there -- and so expanded, uncontested, into the empty north. Where the Vharr conquer by force and the duel, the Niven conquer by politics: annexation, leverage, maneuver, and the art of moving a rival into submission without a blow.
rules: Expansion by political conquest rather than violence -- treaties, pressure, absorption, intrigue. Their hold on the dead north makes them hard to assail, since few can even survive there. As they and the Vharr Empire slide toward war, Marrenhold's neutrality -- and its guarantors -- become critical to both sides, which is the pressure behind the war-summons.

details.Nature: Their name evokes the pale and the snow-bound -- the wan, deathly reaches they alone endure; they thrive where no other creatures can, which implies something uncanny in their physiology or nature. Open: are they spirit-touched, cold-born, undying, or otherwise strange? To be defined if the story needs them on-page.
details.Method: Political conquest -- the cold mirror of the Vharr's martial conquest. They win by outmaneuvering, not outfighting.
details.Open / to build later: What the Niven actually are (nature, appearance, abilities); their leadership; their stake in and casus belli for the coming war; whether they appear on-page at all, or remain a background pressure felt only through the war-summons.
